entry.title: How to get an attractive model. We give a fourth-order Calabi-Yau differential operator, which seems to have been missed by earlier tabulations.
entry.summary:
We give a fourth-order Calabi-Yau differential operator, which seems to have been missed by earlier tabulations. We draw attention to this operator because of its clear geometric interpretation and evidence that it possesses a rank-two attractor, conjecturally giving a new example of a Calabi-Yau threefold with modularity properties analogous to those of an elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$.

Source: arXiv Mathematics (NT, CO, AG, LO, AT, GR) · Tags: #number-theory #combinatorics #high-energy #algebra-geometry

entry.title: Characteristic gluing to extremal Kerr horizons and the third law of black hole thermodynamics in vacuum
entry.summary:
We prove a non-perturbative, non-axisymmetric characteristic gluing theorem for the Einstein vacuum equations: every Boyer-Lindquist sphere in the domain of outer communication of a Kerr black hole, in particular every symmetry sphere of a Schwarzschild exterior, can be glued along a single outgoing null hypersurface to a horizon sphere of an extremal Kerr black hole of sufficiently large mass. The gluing is exact at both ends and matches the full sphere data, including the transversal curvature. This proves a conjecture of Kehle and Unger in the extremal case.

Source: arXiv Analysis, PDEs & Probability (AP, PR, NA, OC) · Tags: #analysis-pde #probability-stats #astrophysics #algebra-geometry

entry.title: Octonions and the Standard Model (Part 15)
entry.summary:
John Baez, Endre Bokor and Latham Boyle have a new paper which gets at the Standard Model gauge group and its representation on one generation of fermions starting from a Jordan triple that consists of pairs of bioctonions.

Source: The n-Category Café (Math, Physics & Philosophy) · Tags: #algebra-geometry #formal-proofs #high-energy
